items.raw_snippet: # Physical Intelligence Secures Over $1 Billion in Funding as Investors Bet Big on AI-Powered Robotics. Physical Intelligence, a San Francisco-based robotics and artificial intelligence startup, has rapidly emerged as one of the most well-funded ventures in the burgeoning field of AI-driven robotics, securing more than **$1 billion** in financing since its founding in 2024 and achieving a multibillion-dollar valuation. The company’s latest major investment came in **November 2025**, when it raised **$600 million** in a **Series B funding round** that propelled its post-money valuation to about **$5.6 billion**. Before this significant Series B, Physical Intelligence had already made waves in the robotics and AI communities with its **$400 million Series A round in November 2024**, which valued the company around **$2.4 billion**. The startup’s funding trajectory has been extraordinarily fast: after a **$70 million seed round in March 2024** that helped establish operations and initial research, Physical Intelligence’s valuation jumped several fold with each subsequent financing, a pace rarely seen even in the fast-moving AI sector.

In the latest sign of intensifying competition, Thinking Machines Lab, the startup founded by former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati, has lost another founding member to Meta. According to reports, companies including Meta, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI are offering compensation packages in the high six- and seven-figure range, with some deals reportedly reaching hundreds of millions or even billions of dollars for top-tier researchers. Google last year secured a deal worth around $2.4 billion to bring in Varun Mohan, co-founder of AI coding startup Windsurf, in what was called a "reverse acquihire" where the company did not buy Windsurf, nor scooped up a stake in it, but paid a hefty fee to license its technology and bring key talent on board.

items.title: 人工智能vs自然愚蠢：为何Gen AI与LLM不会终结人类
items.snippet: LeCun指出LLM只是通往真正AI的"岔路"，Gen AI和LLM不会导致人类终结。
items.raw_snippet: LeCun’s exact framing: LLMs are “an off-ramp on the road to human-level AI.” Useful for specific tasks, a dead end if you are hoping for artificial general intelligence (AGI). She represents a real use case: AI producing consistent content output at a speed no small team could match with human writers alone. Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are a specific type of generative AI focused on text generation. This includes using AI-generated content without fact-checking, using AI-drafted legal clauses without lawyer review, presenting AI-generated financial projections without underlying verified data, and building customer-facing products that deliver AI output without any human oversight layer. The advantage goes to founders who use AI to free up time for high-quality thinking, customer conversations, and product decisions, not to founders who use AI to avoid those things. The rational position, backed by the actual science from people like Yann LeCun and grounded in real operational experience building products like Fe/male Switch, CADChain, and Learn Dutch with AI, is that AI is a tool with clear strengths and clear limits.

items.snippet: The chief executive of the artificial intelligence startup Anthropic met with to...
items.raw_snippet: The chief executive of the artificial intelligence startup Anthropic met with top White House officials Friday as anxiety grows across Washington over the cybersecurity risks posed by its powerful new AI model — worries that have thrown a wrench into the Trump administration’s efforts to cut ties with the company. Neither side made any immediate announcements on whether the discussion yielded a potential truce in a monthslong dispute between Anthropic and the administration over the ethical use of AI, or an agreement on federal agencies’ efforts to gain access to the company’s new cyber tool, Mythos. The meeting comes less than two months after the White House and Defense Department declared Anthropic a risk to the country’s national security supply chain, objecting to the company’s insistence on limiting its software’s use for mass surveillance or autonomous weapons, while President Donald Trump ordered all federal agencies to cease using its products.

items.raw_snippet: Lehane divides the world into two groups of people: those who think AI is the greatest thing ever, and will inevitably lead to a world of abundance and leisure; and those whom he calls doomers, who “have a very, very negative and dark view of humanity.”. “Our job at OpenAI and in the AI space — and we need to do a much better job — is to explain to people why … this is going to be really good for them, for their families and for society writ large,” Lehane told the Standard. Back in 2015, Altman said, “I think that AI will probably, most likely, sort of lead to the end of the world. Altman has also warned that AI could be used to “design novel biological pathogens” and signed onto a letter about the “risk of extinction,” if AI isn’t tamed. Specifically, I asked if Altman had talked about rogue AI or the end of the world on the Joe Rogan podcast.
